metadata.title: First Alert Explosive Gas and Carbon Monoxide Alarm explanation and un-boxing video
metadata.description:
For coupons and instant savings on First Alert Products, visit http://www.firstalertstore.com/store/first-alert-coupon-code-discount.htm today! 

For more information and to purchase this smoke alarm see: http://www.firstalertstore.com/store/catalog.asp?item=1233

This video of the First Alert Explosive Gas and Carbon Monoxide Alarm will show you what is in the package and give you a brief description of the product. This alarm has 3 sensors in 1 alarm, carbon monoxide, propane gas and natural/methane gas.  It also has an electrochemical CO sensor built in which is the most accurate technology available for detecting carbon monoxide.  Our quick explanation of this First Alert alarm GC01CN is provided by wwwFirstAlertStore.com where this product and many other First Alert Home Safety Products are offered.  For more information and to purchase this smoke alarm see: http://www.firstalertstore.com/store/catalog.asp?item=1233

nodes.plm_caption:
This video shows a product demo of a First Alert carbon monoxide detector. The detector is displayed in both the box and the hands of the person demonstrating it. A battery is shown, being replaced in the detector. A piece of paper containing directions and specifications for the detector is also presented.
This is a good view of a carbon monoxide detector, as it highlights the different parts and features of the detector.
At 1s, the detector is shown being held in the hands of the person demonstrating. At 2s, the battery is demonstrated being inserted and removed from the detector. At 4s, a piece of paper, presumably containing directions, is shown.
The video begins with a title screen and ends with an advertisement for the store from where the video was filmed. The store can be found at the website address shown at the end of the video.

summary.brief: A man in a green shirt demonstrates a First Alert carbon‑monoxide alarm, showing its battery compartment, display and test functions before ending with a store advertisement.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a title screen and then cuts to a man wearing a green long‑sleeved shirt at a grey tabletop. He holds a white First Alert carbon‑monoxide alarm, points to the front‑facing digital display and the test, silence and peak‑level buttons, and explains their purpose. He rotates the unit to expose the rear battery compartment, opens it, removes the old battery, inserts the included fresh 9‑volt battery, and snaps the cover shut. He then presses the test button, causing the display to flash (showing a “gas” reading) and the alarm to sound, and demonstrates using the silence button to mute it. Throughout the segment he repeatedly turns the unit on and off, highlights other features, and displays the packaging, instruction sheet and other paper documents on the table. After the hands‑only demonstration, the video fades to a series of static promotional slides that feature the eAccess Solutions and First Alert Store logos, website URLs and advertising text on a white background.

action.detailed: Open the alarm’s battery compartment, replace the battery, close the compartment, then press the test button to sound the alarm and use the silence button to mute it while pointing out the display and other features.
action.actor: the man wearing a green long‑sleeved shirt, whose hands are visible

nodes.plm_action: presses Test button and silences test sound
nodes.plm_caption:
This video features a man dressed in green holding a carbon monoxide alarm and explaining its various features.
At 2s, he removes the battery, replacing it with a fresh one at 4s. He also demonstrates the LED light for the display and the buttons on the alarm.
The background of the shot is a grey work surface surrounded by packaging with paper information and a white paper.

summary.brief: A man in a green shirt demonstrates a First Alert carbon‑monoxide/explosive‑gas alarm, replaces its battery and operates its test, silence and peak‑level functions.
summary.detailed: The clip opens with a title slide for First Alert Store product demos, then shows a white First Alert alarm on a gray tabletop. A man wearing a green long‑sleeved shirt lifts the device, points to the brand logo, the back‑lit digital display and the three buttons on the right side. He rotates the unit, opens the rear battery compartment, removes the old 9 V battery, inserts a fresh battery from the package, and snaps the side clips back into place before closing the cover. Returning to the front, he presses the test button, causing the display to flash blue with the word “GAS” and an audible alarm tone. He then presses the silence button on the left to mute the tone and the peak‑level button on the right, which changes the display to show a peak reading and later a numeric value such as “400”. He repeats these button presses and briefly shows the alarm being turned on and off again, while the packaging, instruction sheet and other identical units remain visible on the dark gray surface. The demonstration continues with the same actions until the segment ends, concluding with the alarm’s screen briefly illuminating and a copyright notice appearing in the corner.

action.detailed: Hold the alarm, open its rear cover, replace the 9‑V battery, close the cover, then press the test, silence and peak‑level buttons while describing the resulting screen changes and audible alerts.
action.actor: a man in a green shirt

nodes.plm_caption:
The person is holding and displaying an electronic device. The background is white and in the bottom left is a website address.
The person is holding a white device with black and red labels, held at an angle with both hands.
In the centre of the video, is a static image of the same website at the bottom.
The background of the video is white.

summary.brief: The presenter holds up a white detector, tilts it, and a website advertisement appears on the screen.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a man in a green shirt holding a small white rectangular detector. Using both hands he lifts the device and turns it about 45 degrees, briefly showing the front, which has a digital display in the upper left, a side speaker and buttons on the right, and black‑red labeling, then reveals the back. As he angles the detector, a graphic overlay appears at the bottom: a logo in black, white and blue above a thin red bar that contains the text “www.firstalertstore.com”. The camera continues to present the device from a few angles while this advertisement remains on screen. The presenter then speaks while the bottom of the screen still shows the First Alert Store.com branding. The video then switches to a series of static slides—a white screen displaying the “eAccess Solutions, Inc.” logo and the website address, followed by a red‑and‑white box with the text “first alert store.com”. The slides alternate without further movement, ending the video.

action.detailed: Hold the white rectangular detector with both hands and rotate it to display its front and back while a website advertisement appears on the screen.
action.actor: the demonstrator, a man in a green shirt

nodes.plm_caption: This video features a product demo of an air quality monitor. It begins with text reading, "www firstalertstore.com Product Demo Video" on a white background and red title bar. The person holding the product is wearing a green long-sleeved shirt. They hold the device with both hands and point to the screen, buttons and other features. The camera then moves to the back of the device, where the person turns it sideways to show the battery compartment, opening it and removing the batteries. They then replace and install the batteries, covering the compartment. The camera returns to the front of the device as they point to the buttons. The background is a grey surface with a white package on the right.

summary.brief: A presenter shows a First Alert alarm, points out its front features, then opens the back, removes the old batteries and installs new ones.
summary.detailed: The clip opens with a title slide that reads “www.firstalertstore.com Product Demo Video” on a white background with a red banner. A man in a green long‑sleeved shirt appears, holding the white alarm with both hands and pointing to the front screen and three buttons to explain their functions. The camera then shifts to the rear of the unit; he rotates the device sideways, slides the battery cover open, removes the two batteries using both hands, inserts fresh batteries taken from the packaging, and snaps the cover back into place. The view returns to the front of the alarm as he again highlights the buttons and display. Throughout the segment the background is a gray tabletop with a white product box positioned to the right.

action.detailed: Open the battery compartment, take out the existing batteries, insert new batteries, and close the compartment securely.
action.actor: A man in a green long‑sleeved shirt (the demonstrator)

nodes.plm_action: Check the detector's digital display for a reading of "gas" and "CO".
nodes.plm_caption: A person whose hands are visible, is holding a first alert device, and turns it on and off. He opens the battery compartment, removes a new pair of batteries and replaces them. He turns the device on and off again, and then repeats this process. In the background, there is a first alert device, in a white plastic package and a grey tabletop and a watch. There is a watermark on the bottom of the frame. Sound is audible.

summary.brief: A person in a green shirt demonstrates a First Alert carbon‑monoxide/gas alarm, pressing its buttons and swapping the battery.
summary.detailed: The video shows a hand holding a white First Alert alarm on a grey tabletop; the presenter, wearing a long‑sleeved green shirt, points to the digital display and the three labeled buttons (Silence on the left, Test in the centre, Peak Level on the right). He presses the Test button, causing the screen to flash blue and show the word “GAS” and later a numeric reading such as “400 CO” while an audible alarm tone sounds. He then presses the Silence and Peak Level buttons, observing the corresponding changes on the display. Next he slides open the rear battery compartment, removes the existing 9‑V battery, inserts a fresh 9‑V battery, and snaps the compartment shut. He repeats the button presses to turn the device on and off, showing the display illuminate, dim, and go dark. Throughout the segment the background remains a dark‑grey surface with the product’s packaging, a watch, scattered papers and a copyright watermark in the lower‑right corner. The demonstration continues with the presenter rotating the unit for a better view of the back panel and repeatedly operating the buttons until the segment ends.

action.detailed: Press the test button, then the silence and peak‑level buttons, open the battery compartment, replace the 9‑V battery, close the compartment, and press the buttons again to show the device turning on and off.
action.actor: A person wearing a green long‑sleeved shirt, whose hands are visible as they hold and manipulate the alarm.

	+ The logo is colored in shades of blue and gray.
* Available At: www.FirstAlertStore.com:
	+ This text is written in large, bold font below the logo.
	+ It indicates that the eAccess Solutions, Inc. store is available at the specified website.
	+ The text is colored in a dark gray font.
* First Alert Store.com logo:
	+ This logo is located at the bottom center of the image.
	+ It features the words "First Alert" in a bold, white font, with "Store.com" written in a smaller font underneath.
	+ The logo is set against a red background.

Overall, the image effectively promotes eAccess Solutions, Inc.'s online store and encourages viewers to visit the First Alert Store website to access their products. The use of a clear and concise message, along with a visually appealing design, makes the image effective in its purpose.

summary_sent_to_llm.description:
For coupons and instant savings on First Alert Products, visit http://www.firstalertstore.com/store/first-alert-coupon-code-discount.htm today! 

For more information and to purchase this smoke alarm see: http://www.firstalertstore.com/store/catalog.asp?item=1233

This video of the First Alert Explosive Gas and Carbon Monoxide Alarm will show you what is in the package and give you a brief description of the product. This alarm has 3 sensors in 1 alarm, carbon monoxide, propane gas and natural/methane gas.  It also has an electrochemical CO sensor built in which is the most accurate technology
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with a title screen and then cuts to a man wearing a green long‑sleeved shirt at a grey tabletop. He holds a white First Alert carbon‑monoxide alarm, points to the front‑facing digital display and the test, silence and peak‑level buttons, and explains their purpose. He rotates the unit to expose the rear battery compartment, opens it, removes the old battery, inserts the included fresh 9‑volt battery, and snaps the cover shut. He then presses the test button, causing the display to flash (showing a “gas” reading) and the alarm to sound, and demonstrates using the silence button to mute it. Throughout the segment he repeatedly turns the unit on and off, highlights other features, and displays the packaging, instruction sheet and other paper documents on the table. After the hands‑only demonstration, the video fades to a series of static promotional slides that feature the eAccess Solutions and First Alert Store logos, website URLs and advertising text on a white background.

Hold alarm and press top button
Press Test Silence and Peak Level buttons

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.

judgement.reason: The video involves manipulation tasks like replacing batteries and testing an alarm, with more than 3 distinct events.
